newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees no need for sugar imports in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees no need for sugar imports in 1997.

text.p: Turkey will produce sufficient sugar in 1996/97 for its needs and will not need to import in calendar 1997, Anatolian news agency said on Friday.
It quoted Selahattin Hun, general manager of state sugar refineries Turkseker, as saying, "Turkey will not need sugar imports next year. What we produce this year will be enough for us then."
Hun said Turkseker, which operates 25 of the 28 refineries in Turkey, would begin producing sugar from harvested beets on Monday at the Elbistan refinery in eastern Turkey.
Turkey had to import at least 350,000 tonnes of white sugar in 1995 after a supply shortfall caused by a reduction in the beet area for the previous season by 25 percent.

Hun said beet area controlled by Turkseker plants was about 345,000 hectares in 1996/97 and that the total beet area -- including land controlled by three private refineries -- was 421,300 ha, up 40 percent from the previous year.
He said Turkseker had produced 11.6 million tonnes of beet this year and would pay 56 trillion lira to farmers for its beet purchases.
"By the end of September all refineries under Turkseker will have begun production," he said.
He reiterated earlier estimates that Turkseker would produce about 1.5 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 1.2 million in the previous year.
Total Turkish sugar output is expected at 1.8 to 1.85 million tonnes this season, compared with 1.5 million in 1995/96.
